questions.q: In the first sitting, what do you do right after writing your questions?
options: Stop, and decide when and where the next sitting happens
questions.why: Coming back after a gap, with sleep in between, makes it stick better than answering right away.

questions.q: Before you look for an answer, what do you do?
questions.why: Asking yourself first helps you learn the answer, even when the guess is wrong (Pan & Carpenter 2023).

questions.q: Which questions tend to work best?
questions.why: Why and how questions led to the biggest gains in a review of 64 studies (Bisra et al. 2018).

questions.q: When you find the passage that answers your question, how do you read it?
options: At your normal pace, going back over hard sentences
questions.why: When words already read were masked so the eyes could not go back, understanding dropped (Schotter, Tran & Rayner 2014).

questions.q: Where do you write the answer?
options: From memory, with the book closed, then check it
As a highlight in the book
questions.why: Recalling beats re-reading in study after study (Dunlosky et al. 2013).

questions.q: How many checks come after the three sittings?
options: Two: a week on and a month on
questions.why: Recall spread over separate sessions kept far more than the same recall done in one go: 68% against 26% a week later (Rawson et al. 2018).

questions.q: What kind of music does the routine say to avoid while reading?
questions.why: Lyrics hurt reading; music without words is about neutral (Vasilev et al. 2018).

questions.q: What do you do in the five minutes after a sitting?
options: Rest quietly away from the screen
questions.why: A short quiet rest after learning seems to help it stick. The evidence is promising but still debated.
